title: The last dark-band residual: a full-depth seam in the rock
question: This is subtle and on roughly half of worlds. Worth a round to fix, or leave it? I have a narrow fix in mind and would rather you decide than assume.
context_md:
**Left tile of each pane is the one to judge** — world x 300..380, seed 5. There is a straight vertical tone edge about a third of the way across, running from the surface down through every row of rock below it.

**I was going to argue this was a shadow and not a bug. Looking at it, that is wrong.** My reasoning was that it darkens rock under an overhang, which is what ambient occlusion does — so removing it might flatten the cliffs. Then I clustered the visible cells and they are not hugging anything: they are **narrow vertical stripes, 1 to 10 columns wide, running from the surface to bedrock**. Seed 7's is a *single column*, 494 cells tall. Nothing physical makes a 6-pixel-wide column of rock darker for 500 rows.

### What it is

The sky/underground decision is per cell now, but the *depth* fed to the terrain grade still comes from `light_datum` — the per-column skyline with narrow dips clipped. An opening clips dips, not spikes, so anything solid standing over open air (every cliff brow) hands its whole column a large depth, all the way to bedrock.

### Measured

`underground_probe`'s `overdark_report` compares the depth the grade reads against how far up you actually walk before reaching a cell the sky can reach. A sealed cave does not count — cave air is not outdoors, so the walk keeps going and the two depths agree.

| seed | over by >=8 rows | >=24 | worst |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 7,569 | 0 | 19 rows |
| 2 | 48,391 | 2,966 | 37 rows |
| 3 | 25,588 | 5,415 | 29 rows |
| 4 | 34,114 | 0 | 23 rows |
| 5 | 25,588 | 2,990 | — |
| 7 | — | 494 | — |

**Cell count is the wrong scale.** The grade is a smoothstep, flat at both ends: 8 rows of excess costs ~1.6% of brightness and cannot be seen. 24 rows costs ~12%, the worst ~23%. So the honest size of this is the `>=24` column — **zero on about half the seeds, a few thousand cells on the rest**.

### The fix I would use

Not the two I rejected earlier. A per-column run-length datum reintroduces bright rock at the floor of every narrow notch, and driving the grade off the sky-light field collapses the lit surface band from 64 rows to about 4 (light decays 0.56 a cell through solid) — a whole-world relight.

The narrow one: store a second per-column datum at genesis — **the top of the lowest run of cells the sky cannot reach**, found by walking each column up from the bottom until an outdoors cell stops you — and feed the existing opening from that instead of the raw skyline. A brow is skipped because there is outdoors air below it; a cave is not, because cave air is not outdoors; a notch still gets the opening. Stored history, no inference, no width threshold, ~8 KB and one scan at genesis.

The second pane is the same frame with the terrain grade off (`F10`), which is not the fix — it removes the legitimate depth shading too — but it does show the seam is the grade's doing.
